title: Impact of fish growing conditions and cooking methods on selenium species in swordfish and salmon fillets
study_system_detail: salmon and swordfish fillets as food products
study_objective: To evaluate the effects of fish growing conditions and cooking methods on selenium content and selenium species distribution in salmon and swordfish fillets.
facility_detail: food-processing/laboratory analysis; fish growing condition is the relevant production descriptor
temporal_scope: Samples from farmed and wild fish; cooking treatments included frying, oven-baking and smoking
focal_factor_detail: fish growing condition (farmed versus wild) and cooking method
comparison_detail: farmed versus wild salmon; salmon versus swordfish; raw versus fried, baked and smoked fish
study_outcome_detail: selenium concentration and selenium species distribution including SeMet, SeCys2 and SeMetSeCys
evidence_passage: Fillets from individual fish under different growing conditions were subjected to cooking treatments and analysed for selenium speciation using HPLC-ICP-MS.
